Thanks. The compiler contract omitted this meaning of the supplied resolution modes. For single, instantiate one match; for multiple, the assigned jointly intended matches. For absent, instantiate the negatives and preserve zero matches. For underspecified, instantiate the competing alternatives and return their eligible union; do not choose between them. A singular request with several eligible alternatives is intentional in underspecified mode, not a design conflict. Likewise, a request whose described target does not exist is intentional in absent mode. Compile the specified world; do not try to make the requested mutation executable by resolving an intended absence or ambiguity.

Please continue the original compilation with this clarification. Keep the supplied writer request, selection conditions and table facts unchanged. Return the complete compilation JSON; report design_defect only for an actual conflict beyond the intentional assigned absence or ambiguity. errors: Design conflict: The selection conditions (membership in #general; user's reaction of 👍 to the #announcements security-audit message; first name Jordan) are satisfied by two distinct users—Jordan Lee and Jordan Kim—each with their own #general membership. The request asks to remove a single specific member, but nothing in the stated conditions distinguishes between these two equally-matching memberships. Any selector that resolves to only one of them would silently impose a surname or other restriction not present in the request text, and a state-changing removal cannot be safely narrowed to an unauthorized choice between two live candidates.
